chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'The people of Mecca do not slaughter (dhabaha) the cow; rather, they slaughter (yanharuna) the cow at the throat (al-labbah). What do you think about eating its meat?' He said, then he said: 'They slaughtered it, and they hardly did anything else [i.e., their method is valid]. Do not eat except what has been slaughtered (dhubiha).'

key_terms.ذُبِحَ: Has been slaughtered (passive participle used in Quran)
key_terms.يَنْحَرُونَ: They slaughter by cutting the throat (specific term)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat slaughtered by cutting the throat (nahr) if the term 'dhabaha' is not explicitly used?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the jurisprudential status of the Meccans' specific slaughter method, affirming its validity by linking it to the Quranic command to consume only what is properly slaughtered. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the permissibility of diverse slaughter techniques as long as the essential conditions of *dhabaha* are met, reflecting the flexibility within the school of Ahl al-Bayt regarding regional practices.
